title: A simple protocol to produce mature human-induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes
protocol: Dissolve palmitic acid crystals in 100% ethanol to prepare a 250 mM palmitic acid solution.
Vortex the palmitic acid solution until completely dissolved.
Store the palmitic acid stock, paraffin wrapped, at -20°C for up to three months.
Dilute oleic acid in 100% ethanol to prepare a 500 mM oleic acid solution.
Store the oleic acid stock, paraffin wrapped, at -20°C for up to three months.
Weigh out 1–4 g of Fatty Acid Free BSA Fraction V into a 50 mL conical tube based on the final volume of 50× solution desired.
Add glucose-free RPMI to create a 10% BSA solution.
Vigorously vortex the solution until BSA is completely dissolved.
Heat the solution to 37°C in a water bath for 15 minutes.
Add palmitic acid to the BSA solution at a 1:100 dilution to achieve a final concentration of 2.5 mM.
Agitate the solution while adding palmitic acid slowly.
Vortex the solution vigorously after addition of palmitic acid.
Incubate solution for 30 min at 37°C, occasionally vortexing.
Add 500 mM oleic acid at a 1:100 dilution and vigorously vortex.
Incubate solution for 30 min at 37°C, occasionally vortexing.
Weigh out galactose.
Resuspend galactose in glucose-free RPMI to a concentration of 500 mM.
Vortex solution vigorously until galactose is totally dissolved.
Thaw out aliquots of 50× galactose solution, 50× fatty acid solution, and B-27™ supplement to room temperature (∼22°C).
Add galactose solution, fatty acid solution, and B-27™ supplement to glucose-free RPMI medium at a 1:50 dilution.
Mix the solution via repeated pipetting or use of a stir bar until completely homogenized.
Filter medium using a 0.22 μm filter.
Transfer filtered medium into a sterilized/autoclaved container.
Cut 20 micron lapping paper into approximately 2 cm squares.
Hold the coverslip firmly and draw the lapping paper square along half of the coverslip 15-20 times.
Move the lapping paper unidirectionally to ensure linear patterning.
Repeat the process for the remaining half of the coverslip using a fresh piece of lapping paper.
Soak patterned coverslips in soapy water and sonicate under sterile conditions.
Incubate coverslips overnight in 100% ethanol on rocker.
Use forceps to place coverslips in proper size cell culture dishes.
Allow ethanol to evaporate from coverslips by leaving them uncovered in a sterile hood.
Incubate coverslips (uncovered) under UV light from the sterile hood for 15 minutes.
Ensure each patterned surface and all cell culture containers are completely dry before proceeding.
Incubate coverslips, after sterilization, in antibiotic-free media without cells to confirm lack of microbial growth.
Prepare fibronectin solution by diluting fibronectin stock in DPBS to a final concentration of 12 μg/mL.
Pipette an equal volume of fibronectin solution onto each patterned surface, typically about 500 μL for large surfaces or 100–125 μL for small surfaces.
Incubate coverslips with fibronectin solution at room temperature (∼22°C) for at least one hour.
Aspirate all fibronectin solution from coverslips and wash once with DPBS.
Completely aspirate DPBS before proceeding.
Warm up replating and cell dissociation medium to 37°C.
Wash cells once with room temperature DPBS.
Add Accumax™ or other dissociation medium to cells (typically 2.5 mL for a 10 cm dish, 0.5 mL for a 6WPW).
Incubate cells at 37°C for 5–9 min.
Agitate cell culture dishes and tap the bottom of the cell culture dish lightly to help promote cell detachment.
Once cells have detached, halt dissociation by adding an equal volume of cell replating medium (RPMI-20 + 5 μM Y-27632 or STEMdiff™ Cardiomyocyte Support Medium) to dissociated cell mixture.
Pipette medium up and down several times to help detach cells and create single cell suspension.
Cell detachment should be visually apparent.
Confirm cell detachment by observing under a microscope.
Pipette detached cells into a 10 or 50 mL conical tube.
Wash plates with additional medium if necessary.
Count cells using a hematocytometer.
Calculate the cell concentration and total yield.
Aspirate medium from the cell pellet.
Resuspend cells in replating medium at a density of 500,000 to 1,000,000 cells/mL.
Gently pipette cells up and down repeatedly to homogenize suspension.
Add cell suspension onto patterned surfaces dropwise.
For large (6WP) surfaces, add 300k–500k cells per surface.
For small (24WP) surfaces, add 30k–60k cells per surface.
Cover the entire surface with cell solution slowly and carefully.
Add additional medium dropwise if needed to cover the patterned surface.
Do not add excess media to patterned coverslips.
Handle cell culture dishes containing coverslips with care.
Pipette up excess solution if it runs off the coverslip into the well.
Use vacuum suction to thoroughly dry the area around the coverslip.
Add back the cell solution onto the coverslip after drying.
Plate cells at a high density to reduce the volume of solution added per coverslip.
Allow the cell solution to sit on the patterned surface for at least 30 minutes before adding additional medium.
Bring the medium volume up to typical amount using replating medium.
Cells should begin to elongate and attach to the coverslip over several hours.
Switch cells to maturation medium 48 hours after replating.
Remove old medium via suction from an area outside the patterned surface in the cell culture well.
Work quickly when changing medium to avoid drying out cells.
Fix and stain hiPSC-CMs plated on patterned surfaces for BNP.
Harvest cells for RNA or protein studies after culturing for the desired duration.
Use vigorous scraping to detach cells from surfaces when lysing.
Prepare permeabilization buffer: Mix 3% milk and 0.1% Triton-X 100 in DPBS.
Fix cells: Wash cells once with DPBS.
Fix cells in 4% paraformaldehyde/PBS for 15 min at room temperature (∼22°C).
Wash cells once with DPBS.
Permeabilize cells: Incubate patterned surfaces (coverslips) with permeabilization buffer at room temperature (∼22°C) for 30 min.
Dilute BNP antibody in permeabilization buffer (1:200 dilution).
Add the diluted BNP antibody over coverslips.
Incubate coverslips with primary antibody solution overnight (12–18 h) at 4°C.
Wash cells with DPBS supplemented with 0.05% Triton-X 100 three times.
Incubate cells for 5 min at room temperature (∼22°C).
Dilute secondary antibody in permeabilization buffer (Alexa Fluor 488 anti-mouse, 1:400).
Add the diluted secondary antibody solution over coverslips.
Incubate coverslips with secondary antibody solution for 1 h at room temperature (∼22°C).
Wash cells with DPBS supplemented with 0.05% Triton-X 100 three times.
Incubate cells for 5 min at room temperature (∼22°C).
Stain nuclei and/or mount coverslips.
Dilute a nuclear dye such as DAPI or Hoescht 33342 1:5000 in DPBS.
Incubate coverslips with the diluted nuclear dye solution for 5 min at room temperature (∼22°C).
Wash cells twice with DPBS.
Place a small drop of mounting medium such as Vectashield® or Prolong™ Gold on a glass slide.
Place coverslip with the patterned side facing down into the mounting medium.
Gently press onto coverslip to remove any bubbles.
Remove excess mounting reagent by vacuuming or pipetting.
Seal coverslip to slide using nail gloss.
Ensure that the cell-covered/patterned side of the surface is in mounting medium (facing down) to prevent cells from drying out.
Prepare bath and myofibril lysis buffer before beginning the isolation procedure.
Isolate myofibrils from hiPSC-CMs.
Prepare myofibril lysis buffer as described in the protocol tables.
Cool the prepared buffer on ice.
Mix the first 5 ingredients.
Adjust pH to 6.8 using pH solution.
Add final two starred components (ATP and creatine).
Adjust pH to 7 using pH solution.
Filter the mixture with a 0.45 μm filter.
Store at -20°C for up to 1 year.
Mix all ingredients immediately before use.
Keep stored on ice until used to lyse cells.
Do not store long term.
Wash myofibrils using myofibril lysis buffer without sucrose.
Remove PBS from the sample using a vacuum.
Add chilled myofibril lysis buffer to each patterned surface to be lysed.
Lift cells from the patterned surfaces using a plastic scraper, passing the scraper over the surface 20 or more times.
Pipette cell lysate into a 1.5 ml microfuge tube.
Vortex the solution vigorously.
Incubate the lysate on ice for 10 minutes, periodically vortexing.
Centrifuge the lysate at 1500 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant from the centrifuged sample.
Wash the pellet with fresh myofibril lysis buffer containing protease inhibitors but without sucrose.
Repeat steps to remove residual sucrose twice more.
Homogenize lysate using a brief (∼5 s) pulse of a Tissue Tearor Homogenizer at 30–50% of maximum speed.
Avoid introducing bubbles into the solution.
Under the microscope, verify that elongated myofibrils are visible along with cell debris.
If using for mechanical studies, proceed to use the lysate as is.
For protein studies, centrifuge the solution at 1500 g for 15 min to pellet myofibrils.
Remove relaxing solution from the pelleted myofibrils.
Resuspend myofibrils in isoelectric focusing buffer (IEF).
Mix the first four ingredients of IEF and filter with a 0.45 μm filter.
Aliquot the filtered IEF and store at −20°C for up to one year.
Thaw an aliquot of IEF immediately before use, vortexing to clear out crystals.
Add final four starred ingredients to the thawed IEF solution.
Keep IEF with inhibitors on ice until use.
